CourseObject:
This course, i.e., Introduction to Computer Networks, aims to familiarize students with the concepts, techniques, and systems of computer networks.

Based on the content mentioned above, student learning objectives are listed as follows:
• Student Learning Objectives: At the end of the course, you will be able to
1. identify the concepts, techniques, and systems of computer networks and apply/modify them for a specific application,
2. assess the system through (performance) evaluation and comparison,
3. evaluate the system using the mathematical approach with the help of performance analysis.
4. build a socket programming program.
CourseContent:
Chapter 1: Computer Networks and the Internet
Chapter 2: Application Layer
Chapter 3: Transport Layer
Chapter 4: The Network Layer: Data Plane
Chapter 5: The Network Layer: Control Plane
Optional Chapters: The other chapters in the textbook
CourseTextbook:
Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach, 8/e
James F. Kurose and Keith W. Ross
Publisher: Pearson
CourseRefbook:
1. Kurose and Rose, “Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach,” 7th Ed., Pearson.
2. Tanenbaum, “Computer Networks,” Prentice Hall.
